summary: Exact open-ended fMP4 edits and finite fixed-audio presentation windows

before.FVID-0403: In an isolated pre-fix source snapshot, both parsers, probe and native playback refuse valid single rate-one duration-zero fMP4 media edits as unsupported duration. Finite-edit parsing/packets/native controls and existing malformed-input refusals pass. Open-edit target: 3 passed, 3 failed. The witness headers have consistent movie/track durations; versions, clocks, trimming and positive CTS are independently authored.
before.FVID-0404: In the same isolated source snapshot, finite fixed PCM/ALAC media edits are ignored: four trim controls expose 60ms rather than 40ms; seek yields 1600 PCM bytes instead of 960. A fractional 44100Hz edit is reported as 60ms rather than 2645/44100 seconds. All three dedicated finite-edit tests fail. Untrimmed controls complete decoding/EOF assertions before the aggregate trim assertion fails.

after.FVID-0403: Admit only the single fragmented open media edit, retaining raw duration=0. A stack-backed resolved edit view derives the composition endpoint from indexed samples and uses media timescale for the open range, avoiding movie-clock double rounding. Playback, owned decode, probe, shader windows, AAC remux and audio planning/export consume the view. Coarse 25Hz and fractional 1001Hz movie clocks preserve exact 20ms media frames; positive CTS and non-sample-aligned audio endpoints stay exact. Nonzero AAC/PCM/ALAC oracles, public WAVE publication, budgets, seek, rewind and EOF pass.
after.FVID-0404: Route finite PCM/ALAC media edits through the existing rational variable-edit scheduler even for one constant sample description. Preserve original media packets and decoder configuration while clipping presentation to the requested range. Native duration, nonzero PCM, seek suffix, rewind, repeated EOF and fractional sample positions now match their owned oracles. AAC finite-path seek conventions and the established leading-empty-edit policy are preserved.
